title.narrative: Spotlight Initiative - Gender Transformative Joint Programme for the Promotion of Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment: Towards the Elimination of Gender Based Violence

description.narrative:
The Gender Transformative Joint Programme for the Promotion of Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment: Toward the Elimination of Gender-based Violence in Zambia is a key part of the broader Spotlight Initiative Sub-regional project in Southern Africa. It represents a collaborative effort among the UN system, national governments, and civil society to address the root causes of gender-based violence (GBV) in Zambia and the surrounding region. The program builds on existing efforts, emphasizing coordinated, evidence-based approaches to tackle drivers of GBV that are often rooted in shared cultural and socio-economic factors across Southern Africa.
Launched in 2017, the Spotlight Initiative is the world’s largest targeted effort to end violence against women and girls. It applies a comprehensive, integrated model to combat various forms of GBV—such as domestic violence, sexual and gender-based violence, female genital mutilation (FGM), trafficking, and femicide. Its strategy includes reforming legislation, strengthening institutions, promoting gender equality, and ensuring access to essential services for survivors. It aligns with the broader goal of achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly those related to gender equality and justice.
The Spotlight Initiative’s model centers around four interconnected pillars: Laws, policies, and data Prevention and social norms change Response and services for survivors Support for civil society and women’s movements
In Zambia, the Joint Programme follows a “whole of society” and “whole of government” approach, shaped by inclusive consultations with stakeholders. This model brings together government agencies, civil society, academia, the private sector, and various UN organizations to develop a unified, effective response to GBV. It acknowledges Zambia’s specific needs while integrating lessons from past initiatives funded by the EU, USAID, and Ireland. Progress has already been made through reforms such as the introduction of Fast Track Courts for GBV and the 2024 revision of the discriminatory Law of Marriage Act. The Joint Programme aims to build on this momentum by fostering a more coherent and sustained national response.
Key UN agencies involved in the program include UNFPA, UNESCO, IOM, and UNDP, supported by the broader UN Gender Thematic Working Group. Their combined expertise and access to global resources—particularly from the Spotlight Initiative’s secretariat—enhance the program’s implementation capacity. It also draws on proven global tools such as the UN Essential Services Package for Women and Girls Subject to Violence and the UN RESPECT Framework for the Prevention of Violence Against Women, which provide best practices for a coordinated, multi-sectoral response.
Each of the four Spotlight pillars plays a crucial role in the program’s design. Reforming legal frameworks and strengthening institutions helps build accountability, while prevention efforts aim to shift harmful social norms that perpetuate gender inequality. Improving services ensures survivors receive the medical, psychological, and legal support they need. At the same time, empowering women’s organizations and civil society enhances community-level engagement and advocacy, ensuring that responses are locally relevant and inclusive.
A particularly important element of the program is its focus on women’s economic empowerment as a preventive measure. By improving women's access to education, employment, and financial resources, the program addresses the socio-economic inequalities that contribute to vulnerability and violence. This intersection of economic justice and gender equality is central to achieving long-term, sustainable change.
Ultimately, the Joint Programme represents a comprehensive, multi-layered approach to eliminating GBV in Zambia. It is grounded in strong political will and supported by a diverse array of partners. By addressing the legal, cultural, structural, and institutional factors that drive GBV, the program aims to create lasting change. Its integrated, collaborative approach positions Zambia to contribute meaningfully to regional and global efforts to end violence against women and girls and to advance gender equality more broadly.
